nodes.content: Human virtue is an operative habit - a good quality that makes its possessor good and his work good, perfecting the rational powers of the soul

metadata.quote: human virtue which is an operative habit, is a good habit, productive of good works

nodes.content: Law is fundamentally an ordinance of reason for the common good, enacted by the person entrusted with care of the community and duly promulgated

metadata.quote: Law is nothing else than an ordinance of reason for the common good, made by him who has care of the community, and promulgated

nodes.content: Perfect moral virtue requires the co-existence of prudence because right choice necessitates both a good intention (moral virtue) and correct reasoning about means (prudence)

metadata.quote: there can be no moral virtue without prudence, because it is a habit of choosing, i.e. making us choose well

nodes.content: The Eternal Law is the supreme type of Divine Reason governing the whole universe, and all other true laws are necessarily derived from it

metadata.quote: The very Idea of the government of things in God the Ruler of the universe, has the nature of a law... this kind of law must be called eternal

nodes.content: The Natural Law is the rational creature's participation in the Eternal Law, allowing man to naturally discern what is good and what is evil

metadata.quote: the natural law is nothing else than the rational creature's participation of the eternal law

nodes.content: Charity is the essential prerequisite for perfect virtue, as it directs man toward his supernatural ultimate end, which natural or acquired virtues cannot attain alone

metadata.quote: only the infused virtues are perfect... since they direct man well to the ultimate end... Such like moral virtues cannot be without charity

nodes.content: Moral virtue consists in observing the rational mean, avoiding both the excess and the deficiency of passions or actions relative to the rule of right reason

metadata.quote: moral virtue observes the mean, in so far as it makes the passion conform to the rule of reason

nodes.content: Rectitude of Reason: The moral standard requiring that all appetitive movements and human acts conform to the right judgment of the intellect

metadata.quote: the good of moral virtue consists in conformity with the rule of reason

nodes.content: Common Good: The universal happiness or shared welfare of the community to which all law and all particular human acts must be ordained

metadata.quote: Consequently the law must needs regard principally the relationship to happiness... the law must needs regard properly the relationship to universal happiness

nodes.content: Truth: The inherent good of the intellect, achieved through considering things as they truly are (speculative) or in conformity with right appetite (practical)

metadata.quote: The good of the intellect is truth, and falsehood is its evil

nodes.content: Justice: The cardinal virtue that inclines the will to render to each person his due, ordering man not only in himself but in relation to another

metadata.quote: justice is the most excellent of all the moral virtues, as being most akin to reason

nodes.content: Right Use of Aptness: The capacity of a habit not only to confer the ability to act well but also to guarantee the correct utilization of that ability

metadata.quote: a habit may confer not only aptness to act, but also the right use of that aptness: for instance, justice not only gives man the prompt will to do just actions, but also makes him act justly

nodes.content: Charity (Love): A supernatural friendship with God that is the spiritual root and mother of all infused virtues, directing man to his ultimate supernatural end

metadata.quote: charity is the mother and the root of all the virtues, inasmuch as it is the form of them all

nodes.content: Systematic/Structural: Rigorous organization dividing complex subjects into numbered points and subsections before providing definitions and analysis

metadata.description: Entire treatise organized under numbered Questions, Prologues, and Articles with sequential inquiry points

nodes.content: Dialectical: Consistent use of Objection-On the contrary-Reply structure, synthesizing opposing views and authorities to arrive at nuanced truth

metadata.description: Every article uses debate structure with objections from common sayings or authorities, then provides definitive answer

nodes.content: Integrative (Syncretic): Habitually melds classical philosophy (Aristotle, Cicero, Plato) with Christian theology (Augustine, Scripture)

metadata.description: Defines human virtue by combining Aristotelian habitus with Augustine's theological definition of virtue as quality 'which God works in us, without us'

nodes.content: Principle-Driven (Deductive): Methodological adherence to foundational axioms, moving from universal principle to derive specific applications

metadata.description: Derives Natural Law precepts from first indemonstrable principle of practical reason: 'good is to be done and pursued, and evil is to be avoided'

nodes.content: Analytic/Differentiating: Rigorous focus on specifying and distinguishing concepts, particularly through defining how terms are applied analogously

metadata.description: Distinguishes intellectual virtues (confer aptness only) from moral virtues (confer both aptness and right use, therefore virtues 'simply')

nodes.content: Teleological: Constantly refers things back to their proper end (telos) as the determining factor for their nature, perfection, or goodness

metadata.description: Defines law by its end (common good/universal happiness) and determines perfection of virtue by direction toward ultimate end (supernatural bliss)

nodes.content: Direct Man to Supernatural Happiness and eternal bliss in conformity with God, requiring infused virtues (Faith, Hope, Charity)

metadata.quote: man is ordained to an end of eternal happiness which is inproportionate to man's natural faculty... it was necessary that... man should be directed to his end by a law given by God

nodes.content: Cultivate Virtue and Right Action to ensure man possesses and rightly uses operative habits that enable good deeds, making him good simply

metadata.quote: the proper effect of law is to lead its subjects to their proper virtue: and since virtue is 'that which makes its subject good,' it follows that the proper effect of law is to make those to whom it is given, good

nodes.content: Establish and Preserve the Common Good through law as extrinsic means to secure peace, order, and universal happiness of the community

metadata.quote: Therefore in order that man might have peace and virtue, it was necessary for laws to be framed... every law is ordained to the common good

nodes.content: Achieve Perfect Rectitude of Choice ensuring human acts are done from right choice, not merely from instinct or passion

metadata.quote: in order to do good deeds, it matters not only what a man does, but also how he does it; to wit, that he do it from right choice and not merely from impulse or passion

nodes.content: Virtus (Virtue): A good, operative habit that makes its possessor and his work good, perfecting a power of the soul, especially the rational powers

metadata.quote: Virtue is that which makes its possessor good, and his work good likewise

nodes.content: Habitus (Habit): A stable quality or disposition of a power, required for rational powers because they are otherwise indeterminately inclined to many actions

metadata.quote: The Philosopher says (Categor. vi) that science and virtue are habits

nodes.content: Prudentia (Prudence): The intellectual virtue defined as 'right reason of things to be done', concerned with right counsel, judgment, and command regarding means to a good end

metadata.quote: Prudence is a virtue most necessary for human life... Consequently prudence is a virtue necessary to lead a good life

nodes.content: Lex Aeterna (Eternal Law): The type of Divine Wisdom, existing eternally in God, which orders and governs the acts and movements of all created things

metadata.quote: the very Idea of the government of things in God the Ruler of the universe, has the nature of a law

nodes.content: Lex Naturalis (Natural Law): The participation of the eternal law in the rational creature, allowing man to naturally discern good and evil and know self-evident, general principles of action

metadata.quote: this participation of the eternal law in the rational creature is called the natural law

nodes.content: Bonum Commune (Common Good): The ultimate end of the perfect community (state) or universal happiness, which serves as the principal aim of all legal ordinances

metadata.quote: every law is ordained to the common good

nodes.content: Caritas (Charity): The theological virtue that is a certain friendship with God, enabling man to love God as the object of supernatural bliss

metadata.quote: The love of charity is of that which is already possessed: since the beloved is, in a manner, in the lover

nodes.content: Passio (Passion): A movement of the sensitive appetite. Moral virtues regulate passions by bringing them into the mean of reason

metadata.quote: a passion is a movement of the sensitive appetite, as stated above (Question 22, Article 3): whereas moral virtue is not a movement, but rather a principle of the movement of the appetite, being a kind of habit

nodes.content: Irascibilis & Concupiscibilis: The two parts of the sensitive appetite that participate in and are obedient to reason, the proper subjects of moral virtues regarding passions

metadata.quote: Fortitude is assigned to the irascible power, and temperance to the concupiscible power

nodes.content: Rectitudo Rationis: The condition of reason being rightly disposed, which serves as the measure and rule for the appetitive part of the soul

metadata.quote: Good, which is put in the definition of virtue, is not good in general... but the good as fixed by reason

edges.evidence: The Natural Law is a participation of the Eternal Law imprinted on the rational creature, drawing all its directive power from the Divine original
Human laws proceed from the Natural Law either as conclusions from its principles or as particular determinations of its general precepts
Prudence requires moral virtues because these virtues provide the necessary, right intention concerning the ultimate end, which acts as the premise for prudent reasoning
Habit is the broad genus for virtue; specifically, human virtue is defined as a good, operative habit
The perfection of moral virtue consists entirely in observing the mean established by the rectitude of reason, as reason is the measure of the appetite
Charity (friendship with God) is impossible without Faith because the beloved object (God/fellowship) must first be apprehended and believed in
In the order of generation (as to acts), the intellect must apprehend the object (by Faith) before the will can move toward it (by Charity)
These two powers are divisions of the sensitive appetite, which is the proper subject wherein the passions reside
The common good is the ultimate end of human action and law, and the good of any part (the individual) must be proportionate and ordered to the whole
The Eternal Law is the source of all order and justice, and the Natural Law is directly derived from it as a means of participation
The nature of virtue as operative habit directly supports the goal of cultivating virtue and right action in human beings
Law as ordinance of reason for common good directly enables the goal of establishing and preserving the common good through legal means
Charity as friendship with God is the essential means for directing man toward supernatural happiness and eternal bliss
The integrative trait (synthesizing philosophy and theology) complements the dialectical method of reconciling opposing authorities
The teleological trait of referring all things to their proper end directly supports the ultimate goal of directing man to supernatural happiness
